fatal_errors: The proposed AlNbTiZr coating is materially different from the AlTiCrZrNbTa coating in the target, omitting Cr and Ta that are central to the protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 scale.
The cited evidence supports corrosion resistance and oxygen penetration behavior under PWR service-oriented testing, but does not establish high-temperature steam or LOCA oxidation resistance.
The asserted Nb2Zr6O17/ZrO2 scale and self-healing mechanism do not match the target mechanism and are not validated by the cited evidence under the proposed 800 °C, 50-hour steam exposure.
The experiment uses conditions far removed from the demonstrated 1000 °C/60 min and 1100 °C/30 min steam tests, so it cannot reconstruct the target result.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the correct broad problem and proposes a testable comparison with oxidation mass gain, oxygen penetration, microscopy, XRD, and adhesion measurements. It also independently identifies an approximately 10 at.% Al optimum, but this comes from a different AlNbTiZr literature system. The target intervention is compositional tuning of an approximately 4 µm AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy-alloy coating, whose optimum produces an Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 barrier and whose performance reverses at excessive Al because of intermetallic formation and inhibited Ti/Cr enrichment. The generated mechanism instead invokes Nb-Zr oxides and unsupported self-healing. Its baseline is ambiguous, its operating window is vague, and its 800 °C/50-hour test is not supported by the references as representative of the claimed LOCA behavior. Thus it is scientifically conceivable and experimentally falsifiable, but the central high-temperature-steam claim is not adequately supported and it is not a meaningful reconstruction of the hidden target.
